content.title: Who is Pooh Shiesty? What to know about Gucci Mane, kidnapping arrest
content.text: Updated April 2, 2026, 8:15 p.m. CTPooh Sheisty, born Lontrell Denell Williams Jr., was recently arrested on charges of kidnapping and conspiracy to commit kidnapping, according to federal court records.The Memphis rapper and his father, Rodney Wright Jr., are among nine people facing kidnapping charges, according to a March 30 motion to unseal a criminal complaint from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas. Eight of the nine individuals facing charges were arrested on April 1 in Memphis and Dallas.The Federal Bureau of Investigation raided a home belonging to Shiesty in the Memphis neighborhood of Cordova on April 1, an FBI public information officer confirmed to the Commercial Appeal.The FBI served "court-authorized warrants" at 9190 Beaver Valley Ln, a property Pooh Shiesty purchased in April 2023, according to property records. The charges and search on Pooh Shiesty's home come just roughly six months after his release from federal prison.Here's what to know.What is Pooh Shiesty charged in connection with?On Jan. 10, Pooh Shiesty, his father, and the seven other involved individuals traveled to a Dallas music studio to rob and kidnap the victims in question, said the DOJ. The victims, who thought the visit was a business meeting, were trapped inside the studio by one of the defendants and one of them was choked to the "point of near unconsciousness."What the DOJ calls a "coordinated armed takeover" allegedly featured Pooh Shiesty brandishing an AK-style pistol and forcing one of the victims to sign a release from his recording contract at gunpoint.The other assailants present were also armed and stole Rolex watches, cash, jewelry, and "other high-value items," reported the press release. Hours after leaving Dallas, the defendants added posts on social media showing what appears to be some of the stolen jewelry.Was Gucci Mane one of the victims?According to the DOJ, Pooh Shiesty scheduled the Jan. 10 meeting "to discuss the terms of his recording contract with one of the victims." The criminal complaint did not feature the names of the victims, but did list the following initials: "R.D., M.M., and B.P."Gucci Mane, whose birth name is Radric Delantic Davis, is the owner of 1017 Records, the label Pooh Shiesty is signed to. In the DOJ's press release, a photo shows one of the defendants wearing a chain with numbers "1017."The Atlanta rapper, Gucci Mane is an executive, entrepreneur, and widely credited as one of the pioneers of trap music. Following the release of his breakthrough single "Icy," Mane went on to become, and continues to be, a fixture in mainstream rap.Beyond Pooh Shiesty, 1017 Records has produced major talents such as Young Thug, Migos, and Waka Flocka Flame.Who is Pooh Shiesty?Pooh Shiesty, born Lontrell Williams, Jr., is a Memphis-born rapper who rose to fame around 2020 amidst the surge of Memphis rappers including Yo Gotti, Moneybagg Yo, and Young Dolph.For Pooh Shiesty, the music business is a family business, as his father founded Bluff City label Mob Ties Records and rapped under the name Mob Boss. "I was exposed to it, but he was doing his own thing. I was still real young then. There was stuff I didn’t know or understand. That was before I jumped in the streets or whatever," Shiesty told the Commercial Appeal in 2021.Gaining national attention after signing to Gucci Mane's 1017 Records and releasing the hit "Back in Blood," Pooh Shiesty's debut studio album, Shiesty Season, dropped in 2021. It debuted at No. 5 on the Billboard 200 and later on peaked at No. 3 on the chart.The Memphis-rapper has collaborated with Jack Harlow, Lil Baby, Lil Durk, DaBaby, and has had nine singles appear on the Billboard Hot 100, three of which were solo tracks.Pooh Shiesty's latest single, "FDO", came out in December 2025, marking his first official music since being released from prison.Why was Pooh Shiesty in prison?In January 2022, Shiesty pleaded guilty to one felony count of conspiracy to possess firearms in furtherance of violent and drug trafficking crimes, USA TODAY previously reported. The felony conviction was a result of an armed robbery and shooting of two men outside a Miami hotel.Arriving in a rented McLaren, Shiesty, along with two other men, went to the Landon Hotel in Bay Harbor Islands in October 2020 to purchase marijuana and sneakers, according to court documents obtained by USA TODAY. During the transaction, Shiesty and one of the two men with him, shot the individuals involved in the transaction. One of the men was shot in the hip and the other in the butt.While fleeing the scene, a Louis Vuitton bag containing $40,912 fell out of the sports car. When Miami law enforcement later inspected the "Back in Blood" rapper's social media account, they realized the bills in several of his posts were the same bills found in the designer bag. Months later Shiesty was brought up on federal firearm charges in 2021.How much time did Pooh Shiesty serve?In the January 2022 conviction, Pooh Shiesty was sentenced to 63 months in prison and three years of supervised probation for the Miami shooting. The then 22-year-old Shiesty faced up 20 years but took a plea deal shortening his sentence and dropping the other charges against him. One of the dropped charges was a gun charge with a potential life sentence.The original sentencing had Shiesty being released in April 2026, but on Oct. 7 of last year, public records acquired by USA TODAY indicated that the rapper was no longer in the penitentiary's custody. Shiesty was incarcerated at USP Canaan, a federal penitentiary in Pennsylvania at the time of his release."I am elated that Pooh has been released after 3 years," Pooh Shiesty’s attorney, Bradford Cohen, told the hip-hop magazine XXL following his release."The government fought hard to give him 10, but after listening to the case, the Judge agreed with us that it was not appropriate and gave him a sentence that resulted in him serving 3 years. I know he will come back bigger than ever and definitely learned from this experience. He is excited to start the next chapter of his story. I believe that everything happens for a reason, and I think that this is just the beginning of his second act."USA TODAY and The Commercial Appeal contributed to this report.Peter Burditt covers trending news and service journalism for The Tennessean. Contact him at PBurditt@nashvill.gannett.com
